pick.name: BJ's Restaurants, Inc.
pick.thesis: Ranked first among today's eligible candidates on six-month return against spy, six-month return against its sector, cash conversion — revenue +3.5% over the trailing year, growth accelerating against the previous quarter, operating margin wider than a year ago, earnings fully backed by cash.

evidence.label: Earnings yield / free cash flow yield
evidence.period: trailing year against the reference close

pick.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +2.9%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $50.75 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-06-30, 121 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 121 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-10-29.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2025-10-30) plus 364 days

pick.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
pick.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

sources.fundamentals: SEC Financial Statement Data Sets (twelve quarters), point-in-time by accepted timestamp, topped up from companyfacts for companies that have filed since the newest data set

stories.title: Google admits AI search makes less money, but it's fixing that with more ads
stories.excerpt: Google's negative cash flow balloons to -$9.06 billion, and stock price tumbles following Q3 earnings.
stories.lead: Google parent Alphabet reported its Q3 financial results on Wednesday afternoon, showing a healthy rise in revenue for the months of July to September. But the company’s stock price has taken a beating, marking one of the largest post-earnings drops in its history. It comes down to several troubling aspects of the new report, including an admission by the company that AI search isn’t earning as much as organic search, and despite that, Google expects to spend even more on AI next year.

stories.title: Do you have seasonal affective disorder? How to tell — and what to do about it
stories.excerpt: The syndrome can make people feel like a "hibernating bear," says Dr. Norman Rosenthal, who published the first research on SAD. He explains how to identify the symptoms and what to do to feel better.
stories.lead:
This story was originally published on Oct. 23, 2020, and has been updated.

When psychiatrist Dr. Norman Rosenthal moved to the United States from South Africa in 1976, he felt less energetic during the harsh winters.

He noticed other people felt the same way. "Just like the autumn leaves, they became depressed on schedule," says Rosenthal. "In spring, the condition reverses itself." He studied the problem, and published the first research on the syndrome and coined the term seasonal affective disorder, or SAD, in 1984.

stories.lead:
Ahead of the US midterm elections on 3 November, President Trump continues to make unsubstantiated claims that mail-in voting leads to widespread fraud.

US states have different voting rules and regulations - but every state allows some postal voting, a method the president says he has used in the past.

BBC Verify visited an election centre in Maryland to get a behind-the-scenes look at how mail-in ballots are processed and counted.

stories.title: Plans for a data center threaten scenic wilderness and dark skies in West Virginia
stories.excerpt: Residents are fighting back against plans for a project that would span thousands of acres near the Monongahela National Forest and popular outdoor recreation, ski areas and dark sky sites.
stories.lead:
DAVIS, W.Va. — Stretching nearly a million acres through the rugged mountains of eastern West Virginia, the Monongahela National Forest links some of the state's best known natural attractions. The vast area ranges from the ski slopes of Canaan Valley to the dark skies of Blackwater Falls and Spruce Knob and includes the small towns of Davis and Thomas that serve as gateways for visitors to the region.

For the past seven months, Kaleb Skelton, his wife, Ella, their 2-year-old son, Ryder, and dog Mabel have lived in a camper in this corner of West Virginia's "almost heaven." Kaleb is finishing a seasonal stint as a campground manager on a lake near Spruce Knob, the state's highest point.

stories.title: Judge orders an inquiry into potential DOJ misconduct in Trump's golf course case
stories.excerpt: A federal judge is opening an formal inquiry into Trump officials' conduct in the East Potomac case, including whether they misled the court about their plans for the municipal golf course.
stories.lead:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — A federal judge is launching a formal inquiry into potential misconduct by Trump administration officials in the lawsuit over East Potomac Park, including whether they repeatedly misrepresented the president's plans for the municipal D.C. golf course.

District Judge Ana Reyes ordered Friday's hearing — the third in as many weeks — to seek clarity from government lawyers days after they acknowledged in writing Wednesday that there is a plan to transform the municipal golf course into a championship-level venue, closing it and much of the surrounding park in mid-November.

stories.excerpt: #5 water polo defeats #6 Princeton, 12-6.
stories.lead:
Princeton, N.J. – Before heading out west next weekend to take on two top-ranked teams, the fifth-ranked Fordham water polo squad took a short drive to Princeton, New Jersey, to face off against another ranked team, sixth-ranked Princeton University tonight. The Rams had a successful venture to the Garden State, defeating the Tigers, 12-6, at DeNunzio Pool.

With the win, Fordham improves to 23-1 on the season while Princeton falls to 20-4.

Junior Andras Toth led the Fordham offense with two goals and two assists while junior Luca Provenziani, sophomore Diego Tresa, and freshman Petar Kulas also scored twice.
